correctness.rationale: Theorem 6.7 supplies exact index-two Gauss-sum criterion and nonzero determinant. For p mod24 equal 13,17,19,23, the eight-unit digit-sum table yields v_p(Gxi)=v_p(Gxieta) at every conjugate; consequently J(xi,eta)/p is an algebraic integer (p unramified in Q(zeta24)). All conjugates have magnitude one, so Kronecker gives a root of unity. Jacobi inversion fixes J under sigma_11, restricting it to +/-p. For residues 1,5,7,11, unequal t=1 and t=13 valuations forbid equality. The exact packaged checker enumerates Jacobi sums at twenty primes using Phi_24 and all eight primitive exponents, and passes. No finite experiment substitutes for the analytic proof.
